source_lock.allowed_data: integers generated from a,b; exact congruence reductions and factorization used only as deterministic sentinels
source_lock.arithmetic_origin: the integer divisibility sequence a^n-b^n and its congruence first-return moduli
source_lock.clock: one multiplication by a*b^(-1) is one discrete source step; no log-prime roof is assigned
source_lock.determinant_convention: zeta_N=exp(sum_(t>=1)#Fix(R_N^t)z^t/t) and the finite Koopman determinant det(I-zU_N)
source_lock.forbidden_data: target zero or prime tables, local Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, prime-weighted global products, log-p roofs, fitted target data, Hilbert--Polya claims, and Route B
source_lock.globalizations: the disjoint union over finite unit fibers and the profinite inverse limit are kept as distinct constructions
source_lock.normalization: finite-fiber fixed-point cardinality and unweighted Artin--Mazur convention
source_lock.object: for coprime integers a>b>=1 and N>=2 with gcd(N,ab)=1, R_(a,b,N)(x)=a*b^(-1)*x on U_N=(Z/NZ)^times, marked at x=1
source_lock.parameter_domain: all coprime integers a>b>=1; every admissible finite modulus N; odd primitive primes and all their powers
source_lock.precision: exact integer factorization, modular order, valuation, permutation, and formal power-series algebra

theorem_ledger.disjoint_union: including the singleton N=1 fiber, the finite-fiber disjoint union has #Fix at time n equal to sum_(N|a^n-b^n)phi(N)=a^n-b^n and zeta=(1-bz)/(1-az)
theorem_ledger.finite_fiber: with L_N=ord_N(a*b^(-1)), U_N is phi(N)/L_N cycles of length L_N, zeta_N=(1-z^L_N)^(-phi(N)/L_N), and inversion reverses time
theorem_ledger.owner_nonuniqueness: finite congruence fibers admit two source-natural globalizations with incompatible fixed ledgers, so the fiber data do not select a single global determinant owner
theorem_ledger.prime_power_lift: for an odd primitive p with e=v_p(a^n-b^n), ord_(p^k)(a*b^(-1))=n*p^max(0,k-e)
theorem_ledger.primitive_return_equivalence: p is primitive for a^n-b^n iff the marked point 1 has least return n under R_(a,b,p)
theorem_ledger.profinite_limit: translation by a/b on the inverse limit of the U_N has no positive-time fixed point and source zeta 1
theorem_ledger.zsigmondy_scope: for n>=2 a primitive return prime exists except (2,1,6) and n=2 with a+b a power of two; this is the attributed classical theorem
